Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
68	
69	| Predicate | Use |
70	|---|---|
71	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
72	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
73	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
74	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
75	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |

79	## Hard repo invariants
80	
81	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
82	
83	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
84	
85	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
86	
87	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
88	
89	**Hard rules**:
90	
91	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
92	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
93	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
94	
95	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
96	
97	### Three-tier user-local override layer
98	
99	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
100	
101	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
102	
103	```
104	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
105	```
106	
107	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
108	
109	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
110	
111	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
112	
113	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 1 first-seed `marimo.toml`: [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
114	
115	**Hard rules**:
116	
117	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
118	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
119	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
120	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
121	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
122	
123	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
124	
125	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
126	
127	**Hard rules**:
128	
129	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
130	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
131	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
132	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
133	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
134	
135	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
136	
137	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
138	
139	**Hard rules**:
140	
141	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
142	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
143	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
144	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
145	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
146	
147	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
148	
149	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
150	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
151	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
152	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
153	
154	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
155	
156	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
157	
158	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
159	
160	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
161	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
162	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
163	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
164	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
165	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
166	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
167	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
168	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
169	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
170	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
171	
172	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
173	
174	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
175	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
176	
177	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
178	
179	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
180	
181	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
182	
183	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
184	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
185	
186	**Hard rules**:
187	
188	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
189	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
190	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
191	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
192	
193	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
194	
195	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
196	
197	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
198	
199	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
200	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
201	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
202	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
203	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
204	
205	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
206	
207	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
208	
209	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
210

```text
1	# chezmoi Source-State Prefixes
2	
3	A practical reference for the filename prefixes (`dot_`, `private_`, `create_`, `modify_`, …) that chezmoi uses to encode target metadata in the source directory, with an opinionated "is it safe to `chezmoi add`?" decision table and a playbook tailored to this repo.
4	
5	## Canonical references
6	
7	- [Source state attributes](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/source-state-attributes/) — full list of prefixes and suffixes, plus the allowed ordering per target type. This is the source of truth; skim it once and bookmark it.
8	- [Manage different types of file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/) — practical recipes, including [Manage part, but not all, of a file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/#manage-part-but-not-all-of-a-file) (the `modify_` pattern) and create-only seeding.
9	- [`chezmoi chattr`](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/commands/chattr/) — toggle prefixes without manually renaming files (e.g. `chezmoi chattr +create,+private ~/.ssh/config`).
10	
11	## `chezmoi add` safety decision table
12	
13	When the live file diverges from the source and you want to resync, the first question is "which bucket does this prefix fall into?". **The prefix changes the semantics of `chezmoi add` / `re-add`** — the command is not a dumb copy.
14	
15	| Bucket | Prefixes | What `chezmoi add <target>` does | Action |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| Green-light | `dot_`, `private_`, `executable_`, `readonly_`, `empty_` | Rewrites the source file with the live contents. Prefixes are preserved. | Use freely. |
18	| Add-safe but re-check semantics | `create_`, `exact_`, `literal_` | Works, but can **silently change the semantic contract** (see notes below). | Use, then `git diff` the source filename to confirm the prefix is still what you expect. |
19	| Do NOT treat as a normal tracked file | `modify_`, `encrypted_`, `remove_`, `symlink_`, scripts (`run_*`) | `chezmoi add` would strip the prefix or overwrite the script body with live data. | Edit the source file directly, or use `cp "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` / `chezmoi edit`. |
20	
21	Notes on the middle bucket:
22	
23	- `create_`: `chezmoi add` **strips** the `create_` prefix, silently promoting a seed-only file to a fully managed one. `chezmoi re-add` is a no-op for `create_` (by design — contents are not managed after initial create).
24	- `exact_` (dir-only): adding a file inside an `exact_` directory is fine, but remember the directory will prune anything not present in source on next apply.
25	- `literal_`: the whole point is to suppress attribute parsing. Adding a new file with the same base name re-parses the prefix — you may need to rename manually.
26	
27	## Per-prefix reference
28	
29	Each entry links to the relevant row in [Source state attributes](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/source-state-attributes/).
30	
31	### `dot_` — leading dot rename
32	
33	- **Effect**: `dot_foo` in source becomes `.foo` in target. Purely a name mapping so dotfiles stay visible in `git ls-files`.
34	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light.
35	- **Typical use**: `dot_zshrc`, `dot_gitconfig`, `dot_config/…`, `dot_ssh/…`.
36	
37	### `private_` — tighten file mode to 0600 (dir: 0700)
38	
39	- **Effect**: Removes group/world permissions on the target. Enforced on every `chezmoi apply`.
40	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light. `chezmoi add` of a file that already has 0600 mode automatically encodes `private_` for you.
41	- **Risk**: This is only a permission bit — it does **not** encrypt the file. Committing a `private_` file with secrets still commits them in plaintext. For secrets, reach for `encrypted_` or a password-manager template function.
42	- **Typical use**: `private_dot_ssh/config`, `private_dot_netrc`, Claude Code config files that contain account hints.
43	
44	### `executable_` — add +x bit
45	
46	- **Effect**: Ensures the target has the executable bit on every apply.
47	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light. Auto-detected when adding a file that already has +x.
48	- **Typical use**: personal scripts under `~/.dotfiles/bin/` (chezmoi-managed; see `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`, `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sms`), helper wrappers, `~/.local/share/tmux-*` shims.
49	
50	### `readonly_` — drop all write bits
51	
52	- **Effect**: Strips write permissions from the target. Runs on every apply, so the file will be reset to read-only even if you `chmod +w` it.
53	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light, but note that re-adding can be annoying because you must `chmod +w` locally first.
54	- **Typical use**: frozen baselines you do not want to edit by mistake. Rarely useful in a personal dotfiles repo.
55	
56	### `create_` — seed once, then leave alone
57	
58	- **Effect**: Writes the file **only if the target does not already exist**. After that, chezmoi never touches the contents again.
59	- **`chezmoi add`**: use with care — `chezmoi add` **strips** the `create_` prefix, which silently promotes the file to a regular managed file (losing the seed-only contract).
60	- **`chezmoi re-add`**: intentionally **skips** `create_` files.
61	- **Refresh recipe**: to update the baseline, copy the live file into the source path (preserves the prefix):
62	
63	  ```bash
64	  cp ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json)"
65	  ```
66	
67	- **Typical use**: LazyVim `lazy-lock.json` (see the [case study below](#dot_confignvimcreate_lazy-lockjson--seed-once-never-overwrite)), SSH `config` skeleton, first-run app baselines.
68	
69	### `modify_` — content is a script, not a file
70	
71	- **Effect**: The source file is an executable **script**. chezmoi pipes the current target contents into stdin; the script writes the new target contents to stdout. Lets you manage part of a file (e.g. via `jq`, `sed`, `awk`) while leaving the rest alone.
72	- **`chezmoi add`**: do **not** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite your script with the live file contents.
73	- **Alternative form**: put `chezmoi:modify-template` in the script body to switch it into template mode (the current contents arrive as `.chezmoi.stdin`). See [Manage part, but not all, of a file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/#manage-part-but-not-all-of-a-file).
74	- **Typical use**: Claude Code `settings.json` (see the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq)), Docker `config.json` proxies, INI files with a mix of managed and runtime-written keys.
75	
76	#### Bootstrap-order contract: `modify_` scripts MUST tolerate missing tools
77	
78	`chezmoi apply` runs in three phases, in order:
79	
80	1. `run_once_before_*` scripts → `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` installs **uv, mise, ansible-core**, plus Linuxbrew (rooted Linux) or Homebrew (macOS). It assumes `curl`, `git`, `bash`/`sh`, and basic POSIX are already on the box.
81	2. **File-application phase** — every `modify_*` script runs here.
82	3. `run_onchange_after_*` scripts → `20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` runs the `base` ansible role, which installs **`jq`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `python3`, `git-lfs`, `just`, `tree`, …**.
83	
84	So at the time a `modify_*` script executes, **only the bootstrap-set is guaranteed**. Anything from the ansible-set (`jq`, `python3`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, …) may not yet be installed on a fresh box. A bare `set -eu` script that hard-calls one of those tools will exit non-zero, and chezmoi will abort the entire apply — meaning the ansible role that *would have* installed the tool never runs, and the user is stuck.
85	
86	**Rule**: any `modify_*` script that invokes a tool from the post-bootstrap set MUST `command -v`-guard it and pass-through the live content if missing. The pass-through preserves the live file unchanged (chezmoi sees `stdout == stdin` → no-op for that target → apply continues), and the next `chezmoi apply` (after ansible has installed the missing tool) does the real work.
87	
88	Canonical guard, lifted from [`run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl:32-35`](../../.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl):
89	
90	```sh
91	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
92	  printf '%s\n' "modify_<file>: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
93	  printf '%s' "$base"
94	  exit 0
95	fi
96	```
97	
98	For scripts needing a python3 (e.g. JSONC handling for VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity overlays), prefer the uv→system-python3 fallback chain — `uv` is bootstrap-guaranteed, so it's the cheap insurance against minimal Linux servers without `python3` pre-installed. See [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl:47-55`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) and [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh:48-66`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh) for the pattern.
99	
100	Reference implementations (good citizens worth copying):
101	
102	- [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl:47-55`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) — `uv` → `python3` → pass-through
103	- [`dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl:28-31`](../../dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl) — minimal `jq` guard
104	- [`dot_docker/modify_config.json.tmpl:19-21`](../../dot_docker/modify_config.json.tmpl) — minimal `jq` guard
105	
106	Failure mode if the rule is forgotten: see [`pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md) — `chezmoi update --init` aborts with `jq: command not found` after `[SUCCESS] Bootstrap complete!` and the user is stuck in a cycle (apply fails before phase 3 → ansible never runs → `jq` never installs → next apply fails the same way).
107	
108	### `exact_` — directory is canonical (prune extras)
109	
110	- **Effect**: On apply, chezmoi **removes** any file inside the target directory that is not present in source. Directory-only prefix.
111	- **`chezmoi add`**: safe for individual files inside the directory, but be aware of the semantic trap — next apply will clean up anything that drifted in.
112	- **Risk**: Very easy to accidentally delete machine-local artifacts (caches, plugin installs) that happen to live inside the directory.
113	- **Typical use**: directories you truly own end-to-end and that are small / stable. Avoid for any directory that mixes managed config with runtime state.
114	
115	### `literal_` — stop parsing attributes
116	
117	- **Effect**: Tells chezmoi to stop interpreting the rest of the filename as attributes. Used when an actual filename starts with something like `create` or `run` and you want chezmoi to treat it literally.
118	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light, but remember the prefix exists for a filename-level reason — blindly renaming it later can break the mapping.
119	- **Typical use**: uncommon. Corner cases like a literal `run_` or `dot_` in a filename.
120	
121	### `remove_` — assert removal
122	
123	- **Effect**: Declares that the target should be **absent**. On apply, chezmoi removes the file/symlink (or empty directory) if it exists. The source file's body is not a content source — it is a presence assertion.
124	- **`chezmoi add`**: does not apply (there is no live content to sync back).
125	- **Typical use**: cleaning up stale configs after migrating tools. Often combined with a template so it only fires on specific hosts.
126	
127	### `encrypted_` — encrypt at rest
128	
129	- **Effect**: The source file is stored encrypted (age or gpg, depending on `encryption` config). chezmoi decrypts on apply. The on-disk suffix is `.age` or `.asc` (stripped in the target).
130	- **`chezmoi add`**: supported (chezmoi re-encrypts), but this only makes sense if you have already committed to a secrets workflow (age keys, gpg setup).
131	- **Alternative**: use a template function (`onepassword`, `bitwarden`, `keyring`, `vault`, …) to fetch secrets at apply time instead of committing them encrypted.
132	- **Typical use**: small number of credential files you want to keep inside the repo history.
133	
134	### `symlink_` — create a symlink, not a file
135	
136	- **Effect**: Target is a symlink whose contents are the first line of the source file (often a template that expands to a path).
137	- **`chezmoi add`**: adding an existing symlink produces a `symlink_` source automatically.
138	- **Typical use**: point a dotfile at an externally-managed file (`~/.config/Code/User/settings.json` → `{{ .chezmoi.sourceDir }}/settings.json`, see the official recipe for handling externally-modified configs).
139	
140	### `empty_` — allow empty files
141	
142	- **Effect**: By default chezmoi removes zero-byte files; `empty_` says "this one is intentionally empty".
143	- **Typical use**: marker files, empty `.hushlogin`.
144	
145	### `external_` — don't parse attributes of children
146	
147	- **Effect**: Directory-only. Stops chezmoi from interpreting the attributes of files inside. Usually paired with `.chezmoiexternal.<format>` sources that deliver whole subtrees.
148	- **Typical use**: vendored plugin directories, `git-repo` externals.
149	- **Companion file**: `.chezmoiexternal.<format>` at the repo root (see [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` in this repo](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) and the section below).
150	
151	### Script family — `run_`, `once_`, `onchange_`, `before_`, `after_`
152	
153	- **Effect**: Source file is a **script** that chezmoi executes at apply time. No target file is created. The modifiers compose:
154	  - `run_` — the base marker.
155	  - `once_` — run only once per script body (hash-keyed).
156	  - `onchange_` — run when the script body changes (filename-keyed; unlike `once_`, editing the script re-runs it).
157	  - `before_` / `after_` — run before / after applying target files.
158	- **`chezmoi add`**: does not apply — scripts have no file target.
159	- **Already in this repo**: `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`. See [docs/this_repo/architecture.md → Auto-run scripts](../this_repo/architecture.md#auto-run-scripts).
160	
161	## Allowed prefix ordering
162	
163	When multiple prefixes apply, order matters. From [Source state attributes](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/source-state-attributes/):
164	
165	| Target type | Allowed prefixes (in order) | Allowed suffixes |
166	|---|---|---|
167	| Directory | `remove_`, `external_`, `exact_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `dot_` | — |
168	| Regular file | `encrypted_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `empty_`, `executable_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
169	| Create file | `create_`, `encrypted_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `empty_`, `executable_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
170	| Modify file | `modify_`, `encrypted_`, `private_`, `readonly_`, `executable_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
171	| Remove file | `remove_`, `dot_` | — |
172	| Script | `run_`, (`once_` or `onchange_`), (`before_` or `after_`) | `.tmpl` |
173	| Symlink | `symlink_`, `dot_` | `.tmpl` |
174	
175	Worked examples:
176	
177	- `private_executable_dot_ssh/private_readonly_id_ed25519` — directory is private, file is private+readonly. (In practice: don't check in private keys; shown for ordering only.)
178	- `create_private_dot_ssh/create_private_config` — create-once SSH config that is 0600 on creation.
179	- `modify_private_dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — the actual pattern used in this repo (see the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq)).
180	
181	If you ever lose the stacking order, `chezmoi chattr` will normalize it for you:
182	
183	```bash
184	chezmoi chattr +private,+readonly ~/.config/foo/bar
185	```
186	
187	## Playbook: what to use where in this repo
188	
189	### A. Everyday configs — `dot_` (+ `private_` if sensitive)
190	
191	Track normally, `chezmoi add` freely, let `chezmoi re-add` pick up drift.
192	
193	- `dot_zshrc`, `dot_gitconfig`, `dot_tmux.conf`, `dot_config/nvim/lua/*`, `dot_config/starship.toml`, `dot_config/tmux/*`, `dot_config/zsh/tools/*`, `dot_config/sesh/*`, `dot_config/zellij/*`, …
194	- Sensitive-ish (account hints, but not secrets): add `private_` (e.g. `private_dot_ssh/…`, `private_dot_claude/…`).
195	
196	### B. Personal scripts — `executable_` (+ `dot_` where needed)
197	
198	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` → `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sms` in source.
199	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` → `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` in source.
200	- Any helper shell script you want on PATH — drop it under `dot_dotfiles/bin/` with the `executable_` prefix.
201	
202	### C. Seed-once baselines — `create_`
203	
204	Files that an app rewrites in-place after first launch, and where you only care about the initial state.
205	
206	- **`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`** → `create_lazy-lock.json`. See the [case study below](#dot_confignvimcreate_lazy-lockjson--seed-once-never-overwrite). Refresh baseline with `cp … "$(chezmoi source-path …)"`.
207	- **`~/.ssh/config`** → create-only template that `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` and ships conservative defaults. See the SSH notes in [README.md](../../README.md).
208	- First-run app JSONs where further changes are user-local (settings files that are a mix of state and preferences).
209	
210	### D. Partial-content management — `modify_` via script
211	
212	Files an app actively rewrites at runtime (adding keys, reordering, …), where you only want to enforce a subset of keys.
213	
214	- **`~/.claude/settings.json`** → `dot_claude/modify_settings.json`, a `jq` script that deep-merges a managed overlay. See the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq).
215	- **`~/.docker/config.json`** → a modify-script that rewrites `proxies.default` while preserving `auths` / `credsStore`. See [docs/tools/containers.md](containers.md).
216	- Rule of thumb: if an app owns the file and you only care about N keys, `modify_` beats a full managed template.
217	
218	### E. Machine-local / runtime / cache — `.chezmoiignore`, not a prefix
219	
220	Do **not** try to track these even with `create_`. They belong in `.chezmoiignore` or simply outside the source tree.
221	
222	- Editor swap / shada / session files
223	- Plugin install artifacts (LazyVim plugin source, tmux TPM repos, …)
224	- Logs, caches, `lazy-install.log`, `.DS_Store`
225	- Per-host runtime state
226	
227	### F. Secrets — prefer templating over `encrypted_`
228	
229	Order of preference for secrets in this repo:
230	
231	1. **Template function** that fetches at apply-time: `{{ bitwarden … }}`, `{{ onepassword … }}`, `{{ keyring … }}`, `{{ vault … }}`. Nothing secret hits git.
232	2. **`encrypted_`** with age or gpg, if you need the value in-repo (e.g. for an offline machine). Commit only after you have `encryption` set and a key workflow in place.
233	3. **Never** commit a plain `private_` file with a real token — `private_` is a permission bit, not encryption.
234	
235	## Refresh / maintenance recipes
236	
237	### `chezmoi re-add` vs `chezmoi add`
238	
239	| Situation | Command |
240	|---|---|
241	| File already tracked, just pick up drift | `chezmoi re-add <target>` (preserves prefix, fails loudly on `modify_`, silently skips `create_`) |
242	| Adding a new file for the first time | `chezmoi add <target>` |
243	| Updating a `create_` baseline | `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` |
244	| Updating a `modify_` script | Edit the source script directly (`chezmoi edit <target>`) |
245	| Changing prefixes on an existing source file | `chezmoi chattr +create,+private <target>` (or `-executable`, etc.) |
246	
247	### Preview before committing
248	
249	```bash
250	chezmoi diff <target>           # See target diff
251	chezmoi apply --dry-run -v      # See what would happen on this machine
252	chezmoi status                  # Which files are in A/M/D state
253	```
254	
255	### When `chezmoi add` seems to have "done the wrong thing"
256	
257	Most often the prefix was silently stripped:
258	
259	```bash
260	chezmoi source-path <target>    # Where does it live?
261	ls "$(dirname "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)")"  # Inspect neighbors — did the prefix disappear?
262	chezmoi chattr +create <target> # Put it back
263	```
264	
265	For a `modify_` target, rewind the script from git:
266	
267	```bash
268	git -C "$(chezmoi source-path)" checkout -- <relative/path/to/modify_file>
269	```
270	
271	## Companion file: `.chezmoiexternal.<format>`
272	
273	Not a prefix, but a repo-level companion mechanism: a single declarative file at the repo root that tells chezmoi to fetch upstream content (git repos, single files, archives) into the target tree. Reference: [Include files from elsewhere](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/include-files-from-elsewhere/) and [`.chezmoiexternal.<format>` reference](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/special-files-and-directories/chezmoiexternal-format/).
274	
275	### In this repo: [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
276	
277	Source of truth for upstream clones that used to live in ansible roles. Entries today:
278	
279	| Target | Type | URL | Previously in |
280	|---|---|---|---|
281	| `~/.oh-my-zsh` | `git-repo` | `ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
282	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions` | `git-repo` | `zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
283	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-syntax-highlighting` | `git-repo` | `zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
284	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions` | `git-repo` | `zsh-users/zsh-completions` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` |
285	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` | `git-repo` | `jeffreytse/zsh-vi-mode` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh` (gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode`, default true; see [vim-mode.md](../this_repo/vim-mode.md)) |
286	| `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm` | `git-repo` | `tmux-plugins/tpm` | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools` |
287	| `~/.fzf` (Linux only) | `git-repo` | `junegunn/fzf` | `dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps` |
288	| `~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb` | `file` | `aperoc/toolkami/main/toolkami.rb` | `dot_ansible/roles/ruby_gem_tools` |
289	
290	All `git-repo` entries use `--depth 1` and `--ff-only` on pull; all entries have `refreshPeriod = "168h"` (weekly auto-refresh).
291	
292	### How updates propagate
293	
294	```bash
295	chezmoi apply                 # normal cadence: checks refreshPeriod,
296	                              # pulls upstream only when older than 168h
297	chezmoi apply --refresh-externals   # force: pull every external now
298	```
299	
300	Externals are evaluated **before** `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`, so by the time ansible runs, `~/.oh-my-zsh`, `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`, `~/.fzf`, and `~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb` already exist. Ansible's remaining responsibilities for these tools:
301	
302	- `zsh` role: install the `zsh` package + change login shell (sudo).
303	- `devtools` role: run `tpm/bin/install_plugins` once (sentinel at `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed`).
304	- `lazyvim_deps` role: run `~/.fzf/install --bin` (idempotent via `creates: ~/.fzf/bin/fzf`).
305	
306	### Nested externals
307	
308	`.oh-my-zsh` and `.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/<name>` are both declared as separate `git-repo` externals. chezmoi does `git pull` on refresh (not re-clone), so the subdirectories are preserved across refreshes — this is the standard oh-my-zsh install pattern.
309	
310	### When to add an entry here vs. keep it in ansible
311	
312	Good fit for `.chezmoiexternal`:
313	
314	- Plain git clone or single-file download, no arch / OS logic other than `.chezmoi.os` conditional.
315	- No post-clone build step (or the build step is idempotent and lives in ansible).
316	- You want the upstream pulled automatically on a schedule.
317	
318	Keep in ansible:
319	
320	- Conditional arch / `noRoot` / `armv7l` skip logic (GitHub release binaries).
321	- Clones whose destination path contains a dynamic version (e.g. `claude-hud` uses `v<tag>` in path and writes `installed_plugins.json`).
322	- Anything that needs `become: true` after the clone.
323	
324	### Editing workflow
325	
326	1. Add / remove entries in `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`.
327	2. `chezmoi diff` — verify no unexpected target diffs (externals don't show per-file diff; you'll see the TOML change).
328	3. `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` — fetch and apply.
329	4. If you removed an entry, chezmoi does **not** delete the destination directory (it's not managed anymore). Remove it manually if you want a clean state.
330	
331	## Case studies in this repo
332	
333	Three concrete walkthroughs of the `modify_` / `create_` patterns above, with the failure modes that bit us.
334	
335	### `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — partial JSON management via jq
336	
337	Claude Code rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` at runtime (adds `permissions`, `skipAutoPermissionPrompt`, reorders keys). A static managed file would produce diff on every apply.
338	
339	`modify_` files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents into stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. The script uses `jq '. * $overlay'` to deep-merge a managed overlay over the live file:
340	
341	- Keys in the overlay are enforced by chezmoi: `hooks`, `enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, `statusLine`.
342	- Any other keys Claude Code adds (model, permissions, `skipAutoPermissionPrompt`, etc.) are preserved verbatim.
343	- Arrays in the overlay replace their counterparts wholesale, so `hooks.Notification` won't accumulate duplicates.
344	
345	To manage an additional key, add it to the `overlay` heredoc in `dot_claude/modify_settings.json`. Requires `jq` (installed by the `base` ansible role). The source file must have exec bit set (git mode `100755`).
346	
347	**Failure mode**: if the live `~/.claude/settings.json` contains invalid JSON (e.g. Claude Code writes a stray trailing comma), `jq` aborts with a parse error and the script exits non-zero. chezmoi then logs `chezmoi: .claude/settings.json: exit status 5` and skips the file for that apply; the broken live file is left untouched for manual inspection. No partial / corrupt output is ever written. Fix or delete the live file and re-run `chezmoi apply`.
348	
349	### `.chezmoitemplates/editor/*` — shared overlay for VSCode / Cursor / Antigravity
350	
351	All three Electron editors read `settings.json` + `keybindings.json` from a per-editor `User/` directory (macOS `~/Library/Application Support/<Editor>/User/`, Linux `~/.config/<Editor>/User/`). Three concerns we manage cross-editor, cross-OS, without fighting each editor's own writes:
352	
353	1. A tiny **universal baseline** (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart accept-suggestion, terminal font) — canonical in [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json). Add a key here and it deploys to all six targets (3 editors × 2 OSes).
354	2. **Keybindings** that should seed on a fresh machine but never overwrite an editor's own additions (e.g. Cursor's `alt+cmd+s`) — canonical in [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/keybindings.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/keybindings.json).
355	3. The `modify_` / `create_` plumbing itself — the bash+python+jq merge script lives once in [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh); each of the 6 per-editor wrappers is a 1-line `{{ template … }}` shim.
356	
357	`modify_settings.json.tmpl` uses an inline Python JSONC normaliser (strip `//` and `/* */` comments + trailing commas) before piping into `jq '. * $overlay'`. This is the only place in the repo where live JSONC needs to be deep-merged in-place; **do not duplicate the script** — extend [`modify.sh`](../../.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh) if you need a new overlay section (e.g. `[python]` block overrides).
358	
359	`create_keybindings.json.tmpl` is seed-once. To push an updated baseline to an existing live file, copy the live file back into the source path (`cp ~/Library/Application\ Support/Code/User/keybindings.json "$(chezmoi source-path ...)"`) to fold in editor-added entries, then edit the template.
360	
361	**Presence gating in [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl).** It ignores both halves of the cross-OS tree on the wrong OS (`Library/**` on non-darwin, `.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/**` on non-linux), then per-editor `stat` gates ignore the whole subtree when the editor's config dir does not exist. Net effect: a fresh machine with only VSCode installed gets Code settings + skips Cursor/Antigravity entirely, no phantom directories. The `private_` prefix on `Library`, `Application Support`, and each editor dir preserves macOS's native `0700`/`0755` mode.
362	
363	When adding a fourth editor (e.g. Zed if it ever adopts the same layout), drop it into the `range (list "Code" "Cursor" "Antigravity" "NewEditor")` list in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` and mirror the 4 source files (`{modify_settings,create_keybindings}.json.tmpl` × macOS/Linux).
364	
365	### `dot_config/nvim/create_lazy-lock.json` — seed-once, never overwrite
366	
367	LazyVim rewrites `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` on every `:Lazy update` and the tracked plugin list differs across OSes. `create_` only writes when the target file does not yet exist (new-machine seed), so subsequent edits produce zero chezmoi diff.
368	
369	**Refreshing the baseline after a deliberate plugin bump.** Neither `chezmoi re-add` nor `chezmoi add` is the right tool here:
370	
371	- `chezmoi re-add` silently **skips** `create_` files (by design — `create_` means contents are not managed).
372	- `chezmoi add` would **strip** the `create_` prefix, promoting it to a plain managed file (defeating the whole point).
373	
374	Instead, copy the live file directly into the source path (this preserves the prefix):
375	
376	```bash
377	cp ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json)"
378	```
379	
380	This is an explicit, opt-in step instead of constant apply noise.
381

383	
384	- [docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md → chezmoi](../this_repo/cheatsheet.md#chezmoi) — command-level quick reference.
385	- [chezmoi docs — Concepts](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/concepts/) — source state vs destination state vs target state.
386	- [chezmoi docs — Include files from elsewhere](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/include-files-from-elsewhere/) — `.chezmoiexternal.<format>` user guide.

```text
1	# Ghostty & cmux
2	
3	[Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/) is a fast, native terminal emulator. [cmux](https://cmux.dev/) is a lightweight macOS terminal built on Ghostty for managing AI coding agents. Both read the same config file.
4	
5	## Managed config
6	
7	This repo manages `~/.config/ghostty/config` (via `dot_config/ghostty/config`). cmux reads this file first (before `~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config`).
8	
9	Key settings:
10	
11	- **`macos-option-as-alt = left`** — Left Option sends Meta/Esc+ so tmux `M-` keybindings work (theme switching `M-c`/`M-t`, layouts `M-1`..`M-5`, fine resize `M-h/j/k/l`). Right Option retains macOS compose behavior for accents and special characters.
12	- **`font-features = -calt, -liga, -dlig`** — Disables ligatures for code readability.
13	
14	> **Note**: Restart Ghostty/cmux after changing the config — it is read on launch, not hot-reloaded.
15	
16	Without `macos-option-as-alt`, macOS Option produces Unicode compose characters (e.g. `Option+c` → `ç`) instead of `Esc+c`, silently breaking all tmux Meta bindings. Alacritty and iTerm2 have their own equivalent settings (`window.option_as_alt` and Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+ respectively).
17	
18	## `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on remote hosts
19	
20	When you SSH into a fresh remote, `$TERM=xterm-ghostty` but the remote has no matching terminfo entry. Symptoms: broken line-drawing, garbled prompts, `clear`/`tput` failures, Neovim rendering glitches. This is especially visible on the first cmux/tmux SSH into a new box.
21	
22	### Option 1 — Ghostty built-in (recommended for interactive shells)
23	
24	> - [Shell Integration - Features](https://ghostty.org/docs/features/shell-integration#ssh-integration)
25	
26	Add to `~/.config/ghostty/config`:
27	
28	```ini
29	shell-integration-features = ssh-env,ssh-terminfo
30	```
31	
32	- `ssh-terminfo`: auto-installs `xterm-ghostty` on the remote the first time you `ssh` from an interactive shell with Ghostty shell integration loaded.
33	- `ssh-env`: forwards `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` via `SendEnv`, and falls back to `TERM=xterm-256color` where needed. The remote `sshd_config` needs a matching `AcceptEnv` line for the forwarded vars to take effect.
34	
35	**Limitations**: only triggers from interactive shells with the Ghostty wrapper active. It does not cover `ssh` invoked inside tmux/cmux panes, from scripts, or from wrapper tools (`rsync`, `aws`, `gcloud`, …). For those, use the manual helper below.
36	
37	### Option 2 — manual helper (works everywhere)
38	
39	A zsh function `ghostty-ssh-terminfo` is defined in [`dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh).
40	
41	```bash
42	ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>
43	```
44	
45	What it does:
46	
47	- Validates local `infocmp` and the `xterm-ghostty` entry exist.
48	- Pipes `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` into a **single** SSH call (no double password/MFA prompt).
49	- On the remote: probes for `tic`, creates `~/.terminfo`, and runs `TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -` — so no root/sudo needed.
50	- Suppresses only the harmless `older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias` warning (emitted by ncurses < 6.3). Real errors still surface and set a non-zero exit.
51	
52	Example:
53	
54	```bash
55	# First time connecting a new box from cmux/tmux
56	ghostty-ssh-terminfo remote
57	# → Installed xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote (in ~/.terminfo)
58	
59	# Verify
60	ssh remote 'infocmp xterm-ghostty >/dev/null && echo ok'
61	```
62	
63	### Smoke-test against `localhost`
64	
65	Yes — if `sshd` is running locally you can validate the function without touching a real remote:
66	
67	```bash
68	# Enable sshd (Linux)
69	sudo systemctl start ssh
70	# or macOS: System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login
71	
72	ghostty-ssh-terminfo localhost
73	```
74	
75	Caveats:
76	
77	- `localhost` already has your own `$HOME`, so this effectively writes to the *same* `~/.terminfo` your local shell reads. Useful as a wiring/error-path smoke test, not as a representative "fresh remote" check.
78	- If you already have the entry locally (which you do, otherwise `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` would fail), the install is a no-op overwrite — still exercises the full pipeline end-to-end.
79	- For a cleaner test, point at a container or a VM where `xterm-ghostty` is definitely missing.
80	
81	## Why the warning appears (and can't be fully fixed client-side)
82	
83	The `|`-separated long description in Ghostty's terminfo is interpreted as an extra alias by `tic` / ncurses prior to 6.3. The entry still installs correctly; the warning is cosmetic. The only real fix is upgrading ncurses on the remote.
84	
85	## See also
86	
87	- [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config and keybindings (cmux runs on top of tmux).
88	- [sesh](../sesh.md) — session picker used in the tmux setup.
89
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Vim mode in this dotfiles repo
2	
3	Catalog of every place vim-style modal editing or vim-flavored navigation
4	is wired into this dotfiles repo, gated by a single chezmoi prompt
5	`enableVimMode` (default `true`).
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	- Default: **`enableVimMode = true`** — zsh / bash / tmux all behave the
10	  same as before this flag was introduced.
11	- Set `false` (e.g. for non-vim friends, CI, the `minimal` Docker bundle)
12	  → modal editing in shells off, vim-tmux-navigator off, copy-mode goes
13	  emacs.
14	- **Neovim is never affected**, regardless of the flag. Neovim is
15	  inherently vim and stays so.
16	- **Editor configs (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI)
17	  are never affected** — this repo doesn't manage their vim-mode
18	  extensions.
19	- Re-prompt: `chezmoi init --force` (re-asks every prompt) or
20	  `chezmoi execute-template '{{ promptBoolOnce . "enableVimMode" "..." true }}'`
21	  for one-off testing. The full prompt text is in
22	  [`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl).
23	
24	## Scope: what's gated, what's not
25	
26	| Surface | `enableVimMode = true` (default) | `enableVimMode = false` |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| zsh OMZ plugins | includes `zsh-vi-mode` | omits `zsh-vi-mode` |
29	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` git clone | cloned (chezmoi external) | not cloned |
30	| zsh `zvm_after_init` rebind block | defined | omitted (no plugin to wipe keymaps → unnecessary) |
31	| bash `set -o vi` (`05_vi_mode.bash`) | runs | replaced with no-op `:` |
32	| ble.sh `ble-bind` keymap (`04_blesh.bash`) | `-m vi_imap` / `-m vi_nmap` | default keymap (emacs) |
33	| tmux `mode-keys` (`common.conf`) | `vi` | `emacs` |
34	| tmux copy-mode bindings (`keybindings.conf`) | bound on `copy-mode-vi` table | bound on `copy-mode` table (same actions) |
35	| tmux vim-tmux-navigator (`Ctrl+h/j/k/l` root) | bound | unbound (frees `Ctrl+L` clear, `Ctrl+H` backspace, etc. for inner apps) |
36	| tmux `prefix + h/j/k/l` pane select | bound | **bound** (kept — prefix-gated, no conflict; vim-letter shortcut is harmless for non-vim users) |
37	| tmux `prefix + H/J/K/L` resize 5 cells | bound | **bound** (kept) |
38	| tmux `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` fine resize | bound | **bound** (kept) |
39	| marimo `[keymap] preset` (`create_marimo.toml`) | `vim` | `default` (FRESH installs only — `create_` prefix means the file is seeded once and never re-touched) |
40	| superfile `hotkeys.toml` (`dot_config/superfile/`) | yazi-parity vim preset (`j`/`k` nav, `y`/`x`/`p`/`d` file ops, `h` parent, `l`/Enter open, `q` quit, `a` create, `r` rename, `v` panel mode, `?` help) — adapted from upstream `vimHotkeys.toml` with `q`/`esc` quit, `h`/`←`/`backspace` parent, `right`/`l` confirm, `v` panel-mode kept | upstream default preset (`ctrl+c`/`ctrl+x`/`ctrl+v` file ops, single-letter focus keys `m`/`p`/`s`) |
41	| Neovim (`dot_config/nvim/`) | unchanged | **unchanged** (out of scope by design) |
42	| VSCode / Cursor / Antigravity vim extension | not managed | **not managed** (out of scope) |
43	| Codex / OpenCode / Cursor-CLI vim mode | not managed | **not managed** (out of scope) |
44	
45	## The gate: `enableVimMode` chezmoi prompt
46	
47	Defined in [`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl)
48	near the `primaryShell` line. The exact prompt text is reproduced below
49	because **`chezmoi init --promptBool` matches by full prompt text, not
50	by key**, so it must be byte-identical across `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`,
51	`Dockerfile`, and `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py PROMPTS`:
52	
53	```
54	Enable vim-style modal editing in shells (zsh-vi-mode, set -o vi,
55	ble.sh vi-mode) and tmux vim navigation (vim-tmux-navigator
56	C-h/j/k/l, mode-keys vi); does NOT affect Neovim
57	```
58	
59	The "does NOT affect Neovim" tail is deliberate — it's there so the
60	prompt itself reassures vim-fluent users who'd otherwise hesitate to
61	opt out for fear of losing their editor.
62	
63	**Three-file rule**: any new chezmoi prompt must be added to
64	`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile` ARG + `dotfiles_init.py PROMPTS`
65	in the same commit. `enableVimMode` follows that rule. Verify with:
66	
67	```bash
68	uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor
69	```
70	
71	(Note: pre-existing `installTunnelTools` drift in the script/Dockerfile
72	is unrelated to this prompt and tracked separately.)
73	
74	**Bundle behavior** (`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py BUNDLES`):
75	
76	- `personal-mac`, `work-mac`, `server-linux`, `custom` — fall through
77	  to default `True` (vim mode on).
78	- `minimal` — explicitly forces `enableVimMode = False` because CI /
79	  Docker doesn't benefit from modal editing and emacs-keymap shells
80	  match what most automation expects.
81	
82	## Catalog: every vim touch-point in the repo
83	
84	### Shell layer
85	
86	#### zsh — `zsh-vi-mode` plugin
87	
88	**File**: [`dot_zshrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zshrc.tmpl)
89	lines ~21–53.
90	
91	The plugin (`jeffreytse/zsh-vi-mode`) is added to OMZ's plugin array,
92	and a `zvm_after_init` hook re-applies fzf / atuin (`Alt+R`) /
93	aisuggest (`Alt+;`) / keys-picker (`Alt+/`) bindings across `viins`,
94	`vicmd`, and `emacs` keymaps. The hook exists because zsh-vi-mode
95	**wipes all keymaps on init** — without re-binding, `Ctrl+R` would
96	stop launching atuin etc.
97	
98	When `enableVimMode = false`, both the plugin entry and the
99	`zvm_after_init` block are gated out. The picker tools
100	(`dot_config/zsh/tools/{05_aisuggest,11_tools_picker,12_television,13_keys_picker,22_sesh}.zsh`)
101	each call `bindkey -M emacs` at source-time, so without the wiping
102	plugin those bindings stick on first source — no rebind hook needed.
103	
104	**External clone**: [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
105	lines ~55–62 — the `git-repo` entry that clones the plugin into
106	`~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` is also gated, saving a
107	network round-trip on opt-out hosts.
108	
109	**Harmless leftovers** (intentionally not gated): the `bindkey -M viins`
110	/ `bindkey -M vicmd` lines inside the picker tool files are no-ops when
111	zsh-vi-mode isn't loaded — keeping them avoids cluttering each tool
112	file with another conditional.
113	
114	#### bash — `set -o vi` + ble.sh vi keymap
115	
116	**Files**:
117	[`dot_config/bash/05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/bash/05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl) (single `set -o vi` line),
118	[`dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash.tmpl) (vi-mode-aware ble.sh tweaks).
119	
120	`set -o vi` is **the trigger** for ble.sh's vi-mode (ble.sh auto-detects
121	readline vi mode at attach time). When opted out:
122	
123	- `05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl` body becomes `:` (no-op) → readline stays in
124	  default emacs keymap, ble.sh stays in default keymap.
125	- `04_blesh.bash.tmpl` swaps the four `ble-bind -m vi_imap`/`vi_nmap`
126	  calls (`C-RET` / `S-RET` accept-line, `C-c` discard-line) to plain
127	  `ble-bind` (binds in current/emacs keymap), so multi-line submit and
128	  Ctrl+C cancel still work the way zsh users expect.
129	
130	**Why both files were renamed to `.tmpl`**: `dot_config/bash/` is
131	otherwise a non-templated drop-in directory loaded by
132	`load_modular_dir` from `dot_bashrc.tmpl`. Adding `.tmpl` to specific
133	files lets chezmoi process the `{{ if .enableVimMode }}` blocks while
134	the rest of the `*.bash` files in the dir stay verbatim. chezmoi
135	deploys the templated file at `~/.config/bash/04_blesh.bash` (suffix
136	stripped) — same target path, same load order.
137	
138	**Out of scope**: oh-my-bash plugins are loaded by name from `OSH_PLUGINS`
139	in [`dot_bashrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_bashrc.tmpl);
140	none of the loaded plugins are vim-mode-related (the `vi-mode` OMB
141	plugin is intentionally *not* loaded — ble.sh's vi-mode is much
142	better when it's on, and `set -o vi` is enough when ble.sh isn't).
143	
144	### Multiplexer layer
145	
146	#### tmux — `mode-keys vi` + `copy-mode-vi` table
147	
148	**Files**:
149	[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl) (line ~68: `mode-keys`),
150	[`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl)
151	(lines ~98–120: `copy-mode-vi` table bindings).
152	
153	Both files renamed to `.tmpl` — same target path on apply.
154	
155	`mode-keys` selects the table tmux's copy-mode dispatches keys against:
156	
157	- `vi` table (`copy-mode-vi`): `h/j/k/l` cursor, `v` begin-selection,
158	  `V` line-select, `C-v` rectangle-toggle, `y` copy-and-cancel,
159	  `gg` / `G` top/bottom, `/` / `?` search.
160	- `emacs` table (`copy-mode`): `Ctrl+B`/`Ctrl+F`/`Ctrl+N`/`Ctrl+P`
161	  cursor, `Space` begin-selection, `Meta+w` copy.
162	
163	Custom bindings in this repo (`v`, `V`, `C-v`, `y`,
164	`MouseDragEnd1Pane`, `DoubleClick1Pane`, `{` / `}` previous/next
165	prompt, `M-[` / `M-]` previous/next output) are templated to bind
166	under the **active table** based on `enableVimMode`:
167	
168	```
169	{{- $copyTable := "copy-mode" -}}
170	{{- if .enableVimMode -}}{{ $copyTable = "copy-mode-vi" }}{{- end }}
171	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} v send-keys -X begin-selection
172	...
173	```
174	
175	The `send-keys -X begin-selection` action itself is table-agnostic, so
176	the same five lines work for both tables. The `prefix + M-y` / `M-i`
177	macros at lines ~147–165 (Warp-style copy-last-output / copy-last-input)
178	are **not** templated — they use `send-keys -X previous-prompt` /
179	`next-prompt` which work regardless of `mode-keys`.
180	
181	#### tmux — vim-tmux-navigator (root-table `Ctrl+h/j/k/l`)
182	
183	**File**: [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl) lines ~181–192.
184	
185	Implements the [christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator](https://github.com/christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator)
186	contract via `bind-key -n` (root-table, no prefix) on `Ctrl+h/j/k/l`:
187	`is_vim` heuristic forwards the key to the inner pane if it's running
188	vim/nvim, otherwise calls `select-pane -L/-D/-U/-R`. Plus 4 mirrors on
189	the `copy-mode-vi` table so the same nav works while in copy-mode.
190	
191	When `enableVimMode = false`, the entire 12-line block is omitted.
192	Consequence: `Ctrl+L` reaches the inner shell again (clears the
193	screen), `Ctrl+H` reaches readline as backspace, `Ctrl+J` is back to
194	LF (newline), `Ctrl+K` is back to readline's kill-line. **For
195	non-vim users this is the more conventional behavior**.
196	
197	Pane navigation is still possible via `prefix + h/j/k/l` (kept, see
198	next section) or `prefix + Arrow` (tmux default).
199	
200	**Documentation cross-link**: [`dot_config/television/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/config.toml)
201	removes its built-in `Ctrl+J/K` bindings to avoid conflict with
202	vim-tmux-navigator. That removal is **kept regardless of
203	`enableVimMode`** — vim-mode users would conflict, and non-vim users
204	don't lose anything because TV's `Ctrl+P/N` already handle next/prev.
205	
206	#### tmux — vim-letter pane select / resize (NOT gated)
207	
208	**File**: [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl) lines ~171–208.
209	
210	Three blocks are **NOT gated** by `enableVimMode`:
211	
212	- `prefix + h/j/k/l` → `select-pane -L/-D/-U/-R` (pane select)
213	- `prefix + H/J/K/L` → `resize-pane -L/-D/-U/-R 5` (resize 5 cells, repeatable)
214	- `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` → `resize-pane -L/-D/-U/-R 1` (fine resize, repeatable)
215	
216	Rationale: all three are prefix-gated, so they don't shadow anything
217	for non-vim users. They're "vim-letter shortcuts" but don't get in
218	anyone's way. Removing them would force non-vim users into
219	`prefix + Arrow`, which works but loses muscle-memory parity for users
220	who *do* know vim. Kept by deliberate decision.
221	
222	If you do want them gone too, edit `keybindings.conf.tmpl` and wrap
223	those three blocks in `{{ if .enableVimMode }}…{{ end }}`. The tmux
224	defaults `prefix + Arrow` for select and `prefix + Ctrl-Arrow` for
225	resize will take over.
226	
227	### Editor layer (none of these are gated)
228	
229	By design, **no editor's vim mode is gated** by `enableVimMode`. This
230	keeps the flag's meaning unambiguous: shells + tmux only.
231	
232	| Editor | What this repo manages | Vim mode? |
233	|---|---|---|
234	| Neovim (`dot_config/nvim/`) | LazyVim distro, lazy-lock, plugins, options | inherently vim — never disabled |
235	| VSCode (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json` → various `dot_config/*/User/settings.json`) | font, line numbers, format-on-save | not managed; install `vscodevim.vim` extension manually if wanted |
236	| Cursor / Antigravity | same overlay as VSCode | not managed |
237	| Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`) | model + tools settings | no vim-mode key managed |
238	| OpenCode (`dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`) | provider, leader key | no vim-mode key managed |
239	| Cursor-CLI (`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) | provider, defaults | no vim-mode key managed |
240	
241	`editor.lineNumbers: "relative"` in the shared editor overlay is
242	vim-flavored display but not vim mode — kept regardless.
243	
244	**If you want VSCode-style vim** on opt-out machines, install the
245	`vscodevim.vim` extension manually. Don't try to gate it from this
246	repo's overlay — the overlay is shared across VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity
247	and the vim extension key would diverge between editors.
248	
249	### App layer
250	
251	#### marimo — `[keymap] preset = "vim"`
252	
253	**File**: [`dot_config/marimo/create_marimo.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/marimo/create_marimo.toml.tmpl) line ~80.
254	
255	Marimo (Python notebook web UI) supports `[keymap] preset = "vim"` or
256	`"default"`. Templated to pick based on `enableVimMode`:
257	
258	```toml
259	[keymap]
260	destructive_delete = true
261	preset = "{{ if .enableVimMode }}vim{{ else }}default{{ end }}"
262	```
263	
264	**Caveat — `create_` semantics**: this file uses chezmoi's `create_`
265	prefix, which means chezmoi only seeds the file **once** (when the
266	target doesn't exist). It never re-touches the contents. So:
267	
268	- **Fresh install** → preset matches `enableVimMode` correctly.
269	- **Existing install** → preset stays whatever it was originally
270	  (probably `"vim"` since that was the historical default).
271	
272	If you flip `enableVimMode = false` on an existing machine and want
273	marimo to switch too, hand-edit `~/.config/marimo/marimo.toml` or
274	delete it and run `chezmoi apply` (which will re-seed with the new
275	template result).
276	
277	Why not `modify_` instead? Because marimo writes its own settings
278	(theme, recent files, snippet paths) into the same file via the web
279	UI, and a `modify_` script would have to reconcile those — overkill
280	for one keymap key.
281	
282	#### superfile — `hotkeys.toml` preset swap
283	
284	**File**: [`dot_config/superfile/hotkeys.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/superfile/hotkeys.toml.tmpl).
285	
286	Superfile (`spf`) is a TUI file manager. There is no runtime
287	`vim_mode` flag in `config.toml` — upstream ships **two** separate
288	preset files (`hotkeys.toml` default, `vimHotkeys.toml`) and the
289	README literally says "If you are vim/nvim user please change your
290	default hotkeys config to vim version". The chezmoi template
291	swaps the full body based on `enableVimMode`:
292	
293	- **`true`** → upstream `vimHotkeys.toml` body with four yazi-parity
294	  tweaks: `quit = ['q', 'esc']` (vs upstream vim `ctrl+c`),
295	  `parent_directory = ['h', 'left', 'backspace']` (vs upstream vim
296	  `-` only), `confirm = ['enter', 'right', 'l']` (vs upstream vim
297	  `enter` only), `change_panel_mode = ['v', '']` (vs upstream vim
298	  `m`). `close_file_panel` lands on `w` since `q` is reclaimed for
299	  quit.
300	- **`false`** → upstream `hotkeys.toml` verbatim. File ops are
301	  Ctrl-prefixed (`copy_items = ['ctrl+c', '']`,
302	  `paste_items = ['ctrl+v', 'ctrl+w', '']`); the default already
303	  includes `j`/`k`/`l`/`h` as *secondary* nav bindings, so non-vim
304	  users keep optional vim nav without disruptive single-letter
305	  file ops.
306	
307	**Path note**: superfile honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` on macOS too
308	(verified via `spf pl` → `~/.config/superfile/hotkeys.toml`), so a
309	single source path under `dot_config/superfile/` covers macOS and
310	Linux. No `private_Library/private_Application Support/` branch
311	needed despite Go's `os.UserConfigDir()` defaulting to
312	`~/Library/Application Support` on Darwin — superfile resolves the
313	path itself.
314	
315	**Forbidden bindings** (per upstream docs): `Ctrl+M` conflicts with
316	Enter, `Ctrl+I` with Tab, `Ctrl+?` / `Ctrl+[` with Delete/Backspace.
317	Both preset bodies in the template avoid these.
318	
319	**Re-sync**: bodies pinned via comment to
320	`yorukot/superfile @ main` snapshot date. Re-fetch
321	`src/superfile_config/hotkeys.toml` + `vimHotkeys.toml` when
322	bumping.
323	
324	#### Other tools
325	
326	Spot-checked and confirmed **not** managed (or no vim keys present):
327	
328	- `lazygit` (`dot_config/lazygit/config.yml`) — only sets the delta
329	  pager. No `keybindings:` block. Defaults are vim-flavored upstream
330	  but that's not in this repo's surface area.
331	- `yazi` (`dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml`) — empty stub, no managed
332	  keybindings.
333	- `lf`, `ranger`, `broot` — no configs in this repo.
334	- `fzf` (`dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh`) — `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS` has no
335	  `--bind` for vi keys; default emacs-style.
336	- `less`, `bat`, `delta` — no `LESS=…` vi-keys env, no managed
337	  `~/.lesskey`.
338	- `k9s`, `btop`, `htop`, `lazydocker`, `gh-dash` — not managed by
339	  this repo.
340	- `television` — global keymap is Ctrl-style; channel-specific
341	  configs use Alt+letter, no vi keys.
342	- `zellij` — uses `default_mode "locked"`, all keys pass through to
343	  inner apps; nothing to disable.
344	- `claude-code` (`~/.claude/keybindings.json` overlay) — uses Ctrl-style
345	  keys (`Ctrl+R`, `Ctrl+T`, `Ctrl+G`, `Ctrl+S`, `Shift+Tab`); no vim
346	  bindings managed.
347	
348	If a future tool gains managed vim keybindings, add a row to the
349	catalog table above and update [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/AGENTS.md)'s
350	"Hard repo invariant: `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT
351	Neovim" section in the same commit.
352	
353	## What happens when you flip `enableVimMode = false`
354	
355	After `chezmoi apply`:
356	
357	- `~/.zshrc` no longer contains `zsh-vi-mode` in `plugins=(...)` and
358	  the `zvm_after_init` block is gone.
359	- `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode/` is **not** cloned (the
360	  externals stanza is templated out — saves a network round-trip).
361	- `~/.config/bash/05_vi_mode.bash` body is `: # vim mode disabled by chezmoi enableVimMode=false`
362	  → readline + ble.sh stay in default emacs keymap.
363	- `~/.config/bash/04_blesh.bash` binds `Ctrl+RET` / `Shift+RET` /
364	  `Ctrl+C` on the default keymap (no `-m vi_imap` / `-m vi_nmap`).
365	- `~/.config/tmux/common.conf` has `setw -g mode-keys emacs`.
366	- `~/.config/tmux/keybindings.conf` has `bind -T copy-mode v send-keys -X begin-selection`
367	  (etc.) **and no `bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell ...`** vim-tmux-navigator
368	  bindings.
369	- (FRESH installs only) `~/.config/marimo/marimo.toml` has
370	  `preset = "default"`.
371	- `~/.config/superfile/hotkeys.toml` has upstream default body
372	  (Ctrl-prefixed file ops, `j`/`k`/`l`/`h` as secondary nav).
373	
374	**Behavioral consequences inside tmux**:
375	
376	- `Ctrl+L` clears the inner shell screen again (no longer captured
377	  by vim-tmux-navigator).
378	- `Ctrl+H` is backspace at the prompt.
379	- `Ctrl+J` is plain LF (newline).
380	- `Ctrl+K` is `kill-line` in readline (zle line-end-killer in zsh).
381	- Inside tmux copy-mode: `Space` starts selection, `Meta+w` copies,
382	  `Ctrl+B`/`Ctrl+F` move cursor — instead of `v`/`y`/`h`/`l`.
383	- Pane navigation: `prefix + h/j/k/l` still works (kept). Use
384	  `prefix + Arrow` if you don't want vim letters.
385	
386	## How to opt out (existing install)
387	
388	```bash
389	# Re-prompt for everything (you'll be asked enableVimMode plus ~22 others):
390	chezmoi init --force
391	
392	# Or just edit the data file by hand:
393	$EDITOR ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml
394	# change: enableVimMode = false
395	chezmoi apply
396	
397	# Reload the active session(s):
398	exec zsh                # or: exec bash
399	tmux kill-server        # then start a fresh tmux
400	```
401	
402	If you want a side-by-side preview of what would change before
403	committing to apply:
404	
405	```bash
406	chezmoi diff             # shows everything
407	chezmoi diff dot_config/tmux dot_config/bash dot_zshrc \
408	             .chezmoiexternal.toml dot_config/marimo \
409	             dot_config/superfile
410	```
411	
412	**Verify on a single host without affecting others**: this is the
413	ideal use of `just fleet-status` (read-only readiness probe per host)
414	and `just fleet-apply --hosts <one-host>` to roll out the change
415	gradually. See [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](fleet-apply.md).
416	
417	## How to opt back in
418	
419	Same flow with the value flipped:
420	
421	```bash
422	$EDITOR ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml   # set enableVimMode = true
423	chezmoi apply
424	exec zsh
425	tmux kill-server
426	```
427	
428	The first apply will:
429	
430	- re-clone `zsh-vi-mode` into `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/`
431	  (chezmoi external),
432	- re-add the plugin name to `~/.zshrc`,
433	- restore `set -o vi` in bash,
434	- swap tmux `mode-keys` back to `vi`,
435	- restore the 12 vim-tmux-navigator lines.
436	
437	Marimo's `create_marimo.toml` will **not** auto-flip back — `create_`
438	files seed once. To force a re-seed, delete `~/.config/marimo/marimo.toml`
439	first, then `chezmoi apply`.
440	
441	## For maintainers: adding a new vim-touched config
442	
443	If you add a new app config that has a vim/emacs choice, decide first
444	whether it belongs under `enableVimMode`'s umbrella:
445	
446	**Yes, gate it** if all of:
447	
448	- It's a TUI / multiplexer / shell-adjacent tool (not a heavyweight
449	  GUI editor).
450	- A non-vim user would actively suffer if vim-mode is left on.
451	- The setting can be templated cleanly (i.e. the file is already
452	  `.tmpl` or it's reasonable to make it one).
453	
454	Then:
455	
456	1. Edit the relevant config to template the vim/emacs choice on
457	   `{{ if .enableVimMode }}` — rename the file to `.tmpl` if needed.
458	2. Add a row to the catalog table at the top of this doc.
459	3. Update the corresponding tool doc (e.g. `docs/tools/<tool>.md`) to
460	   note the gating.
461	4. If the gating is non-trivial (e.g. a `create_` file that won't
462	   auto-migrate), add a "Hard repo invariant" entry in
463	   [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
464	   under the existing "`enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT
465	   Neovim" section.
466	
467	**No, leave it alone** if any of:
468	
469	- It's an editor / IDE (VSCode, Cursor, Codex TUI, OpenCode TUI,
470	  Neovim) — separate concern, users may want vim in their editor
471	  even if they don't want it in their shell.
472	- The setting is buried in a `modify_` script that hand-merges live
473	  state — gating would risk corrupting user-edited keys.
474	- The default behavior is identical for vim and non-vim users (no
475	  conflict either way).
476	
477	When in doubt: **don't gate**. The flag's semantic is "shells + tmux";
478	expanding it case-by-case keeps the contract clear.
479

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
52	  move on
